title: Arrangers in Hampton's band: Milton Buckner, Al Hayes, Joe Morris
summary: Buckner wrote most of the band's arrangements, Al Hayes wrote Loose Wigs, and Joe Morris wrote Chop-Chop.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: (Side 6)
What do you want from here
No, but you keep pulling the table, and I'm afraid you'll pull it out of the wall.
Do I know where I'm taking up from now? Do you know --

Well, what I want you to do on that is tell a little bit more about that Lionel Hampton band. You know, that was an important band at that time. And I mean who did most of the arranging. Things like that, you see.

Well, Milton Buckner was one of the main arrangers in the band. He did most of it. Al Hayes did a couple of tunes in the band. Joe Morris did the Chop-Chop, if you remember, on the flip side of Hamp's Boogie Woogie.
Yeah, Chop-Chop.
We had other arrangers to come in to do vocal (inaudible).
Which arrangements did Al Hayes do? Do you remember?
Pardon?
Which arrangements did Al Hayes do? Do you remember?
Al Hayes had an arrangement in there called Loose Wigs.
Called what?
Loose Wigs.
Oh, Loose Wigs.
Remember Loose Wigs?
Yeah, that's a nice one.

That was Al Hayes. And that's what he was Loose Wigs. Just as stone nuts as he could be, and the tune was -- ta-ta-doo-da-dee-da,(et cetera), Loose Wigs, you know, and that's the way he is. But he was a character.
(Laughter)
But Milt did most of the writing. Of course, Milt got no credit for anything he did.
